raw:
You leave Bea’s loan agreement where Nell files it and do not approach the locked cupboard.

At the worktable, Nell gives you a pencil, numbered slips and the first section of the business-paper box.

“Keep the existing order. Record it before you decide whether it makes sense. These first items all fall under the 2024 transfer, so their legal status is trust-owned. Other fields may still be uncertain.”

You begin with the electricity invoice she demonstrated. The next papers are a printer’s bill for weekly listings, a distributor’s letter changing a booking date and an estimate for patching water damage above the auditorium. You record dates and creators where they appear, describe folds and rust staining without attempting repairs, and identify the box and transfer schedule as the source of provenance.

A run of twelve utility bills stays together as one file rather than becoming twelve separate catalogue entries. Nell shows you how to describe the date range and note a missing month without claiming that the invoice itself never existed.

Halfway down the stack, you find several old staff rotas containing surnames, telephone numbers and handwritten notes about absences. The cinema owns the paper, but the personal information affects access. You mark the file for restricted review and take the query downstairs rather than leaving it open on the table.

Nell reads the slip in the office.

“Correct. Ownership doesn’t make personal data public. Put these in the temporary restricted folder, and I’ll set an access period after checking the dates.”

Back upstairs, you continue. An unsigned maintenance note has no reliable author, so the creator remains unidentified. A letter with an illegible date is recorded as undated rather than assigned a year from the papers around it. Nothing is copied, scanned or diverted towards the reopening display.

When Nell returns to review the first entries, she checks each against the documents and the transfer schedule.

“You’ve kept the unknowns visible,” she says. “That’s usable cataloguing.”

She makes one small addition to the condition vocabulary—distinguishing inactive rust staining from a fastener still damaging the paper—then leaves you with the next folder in the assigned box.

The archive room settles into steady work: paper lifted and replaced, catalogue fields completed, numbered slips laid beside each finished group. The green photograph album remains secured in the loan cupboard across the room.
